title.zh: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁
title.en: Volume 464 Biographies 251: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijingzi, Ren Zhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong with: Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, Kang Guangren
title.raw: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁

sentences.zh: 李端棻 徐致靖（子仁鑄） 陳寶箴 黃遵憲 曾鉌 楊深秀 楊銳 劉光第 譚嗣同 唐才常 林旭 康廣仁 李端棻 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing (son Ren Zhu), Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Zeng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, courtesy name [Biyuan], a native of [Guizhu].
translations.idiomatic: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing (whose son was Ren Zhu), Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Zeng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, whose courtesy name was Biyuan, was a native of Guizhu.

sentences.zh: 二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為大學士、尚書所器。

translations.literal: In the second year [of Guangxu] he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler in the Hanlin Academy, was appointed reviser, and was esteemed by Grand Secretary Wo Ren and Minister Luo Dunyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, and was appointed reviser; Grand Secretary Wo Ren and Minister Luo Dunyan both valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 十年，出督學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was sent out to serve as educational commissioner for Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 值寇亂後，荒服道亙，前使者試未遍，始一一按臨，文化漸振。

translations.literal: It fell in the aftermath of the rebellion; the remote regions were cut off on every road, and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations everywhere. Duanfen now went in person to each place in turn, and culture gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: This was just after the rebellion, when the frontier districts were still cut off and the previous commissioner had not been able to examine candidates throughout the province. Duanfen now toured each district in person, and learning and culture gradually recovered.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉御史，以叔父官京尹，迴避，改故官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to censor; because his uncle held the post of metropolitan magistrate he withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest and returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made a censor, but because his uncle was serving as metropolitan magistrate he had to withdraw for avoidance and was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to become a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 越六年，調倉場。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was transferred to oversee the grain depots.

sentences.zh: 前後迭司文柄，四為鄉試考官，一為會試副總裁，喜獎拔士類。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly held literary authority: four times as examiner for the provincial examinations and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination; he delighted in encouraging and advancing men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: He held literary office again and again—four times as provincial examiner and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination—and took pleasure in discovering and promoting talented scholars.

sentences.zh: 典試，賞才，以從妹妻之，自是頗納議，娓娓道東西邦制度。

translations.literal: When he presided over the examination in Guangdong he admired Liang Qichao's talent and gave him his younger cousin in marriage; from then on he often accepted Liang's counsel and would speak at length of the institutions of Eastern and Western countries.
translations.idiomatic: While examining candidates in Guangdong he recognized Liang Qichao's ability, gave him his younger cousin in marriage, and thereafter often took Liang's advice, discoursing at length on the political systems of East and West.

sentences.zh: 維時上書請變法，兼及興學。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei memorialized requesting reform and also urged the promotion of education.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials calling for reform and for the expansion of schooling.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遂疏請立京師大學，凡各省府、州、縣遍設學堂，分齋講習；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Duanfen then memorialized requesting the establishment of a national university in the capital and schools in every prefecture, department, and county of each province, with separate halls for instruction;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Duanfen memorialized for a national university in the capital and schools in every prefecture, department, and county, each with separate halls for study;

sentences.zh: 並建藏書樓、儀器院、譯書局，廣立報館，選派遊歷生。

translations.literal: and also the building of libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, the wide establishment of newspapers, and the selection and dispatch of students to travel abroad.
translations.idiomatic: together with libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, more newspapers, and students selected to travel abroad.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，密薦及堪大用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as men capable of high responsibility.

sentences.zh: 又以各衙門則例，語涉紛歧，疏請刪訂，上尤善之，詔趣各長官定限期革前敝。

translations.literal: He also noted that the regulations of the various yamen were worded in conflicting ways and memorialized requesting their revision and abridgment; the emperor especially approved this and ordered each chief official to set a deadline for reforming past abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He also pointed out that the regulations of the various ministries were inconsistent and asked that they be revised; the emperor especially approved, and ordered each department head to set a deadline for abolishing old abuses.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，等敗，自疏檢舉，詔褫職，戍。

translations.literal: Before long Kang Youwei and his party were defeated; Duanfen memorialized to accuse himself, and an edict stripped him of office and sent him into exile on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kang Youwei's faction fell; Duanfen reported on himself in a memorial, was stripped of office by edict, and was banished to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 中道遘疾，留。

translations.literal: On the way he fell ill and remained at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road and was detained at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，赦歸，主講。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was pardoned and returned home, and lectured at the Jingshi Academy in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was pardoned and returned home to lecture at the Jingshi Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-third year.

sentences.zh: 元年，從、京朝官請，復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, at the request of officials from Yunnan and Guizhou in the capital, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign, at the petition of capital officials from Yunnan and Guizhou, his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 徐致靖（子仁鑄） ，字，人，寄籍。

translations.literal: Xu Zhijing (son Ren Zhu), courtesy name [Zijing], a native of [Yixing in Jiangsu], with registered domicile elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijing (whose son was Ren Zhu), whose courtesy name was Zijing, was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu and was registered under another domicile.

sentences.zh: 二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to reader in waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to reader in waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，二十三年，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father was completed, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After his period of mourning for his father ended, he was recalled in the twenty-third year to his former post.

sentences.zh: 嘗憂外患日迫，思所以為獻納計。

translations.literal: Zhijing had long worried that foreign danger was pressing daily and thought how he might offer counsel to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been troubled by the daily tightening of foreign pressure and pondered how he might advise the throne.

sentences.zh: 子，時以編修督學，倡新學，書告舉。

translations.literal: His son Ren Zhu, then serving as reviser and educational commissioner in Hunan, promoted the new learning and wrote urging his father to recommend Kang Youwei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren Zhu, then a reviser serving as Hunan's educational commissioner, was promoting the new learning and wrote urging his father to recommend Kang Youwei.

sentences.zh: 遂上言：「國是未定，請申乾斷示從違。

translations.literal: Zhijing then memorialized: "The national policy is not yet settled; I beg that Your Majesty's own decision be announced to show what is to be followed or rejected."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I beg that Your Majesty's own decision be made clear, so all may know what to follow or reject."

sentences.zh: 」藉以覘上意。

translations.literal: Thus he sought to gauge the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he hoped to discern the emperor's true intentions.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔果求通才，於是奏堪大用，並及、等。

translations.literal: Before long an edict did indeed call for men of outstanding talent; Zhijing then memorialized that Kang Youwei was fit for great employment, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict did call for men of talent; Zhijing then memorialized that Kang Youwei was fit for high office, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 又連上書請廢製藝，改試策論，省冗官，酌置散卿。

translations.literal: He also submitted repeated memorials requesting the abolition of the examination essay on the classics, the substitution of policy dissertations, the reduction of superfluous officials, and the measured establishment of honorary grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent repeated memorials asking to abolish the eight-legged essay, test candidates on policy essays instead, cut redundant offices, and create appropriate honorary posts.

sentences.zh: 復以邊患棘，宜練重兵，力荐主軍事。

translations.literal: He further urged that with border troubles acute, heavy troops should be trained and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to command military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued that with border troubles acute, the empire should train substantial forces, and he strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to take charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上皆然其言，敕依行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all these proposals and ordered them carried out.

sentences.zh: 罷斥禮部尚書等阻遏言路，遂命權右侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who blocked the channels of remonstrance were dismissed; Zhijing was then ordered to act as vice minister on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who had blocked memorials to the throne were removed, and Zhijing was ordered to serve as acting vice minister on the right.

sentences.zh: 二十四年八月，太后復出訓政，參預新政諸臣皆獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the Empress Dowager resumed regency; all who had taken part in the new policies were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the Empress Dowager resumed regency, and all who had taken part in the new policies were punished.

sentences.zh: 褫職坐系，尋定永遠監禁，亦罷官。

translations.literal: Zhijing was stripped of office and imprisoned; he was soon sentenced to perpetual confinement, and Ren Zhu was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing was stripped of office and imprisoned, soon sentenced to perpetual confinement; Ren Zhu was also dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 庚子，聯軍陷京師，始出獄待罪，詔赦免。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies took the capital, he was released from prison to await judgment and was pardoned by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies occupied the capital, he was released from prison to await judgment and was pardoned by edict.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 陳寶箴 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Chen Baozhen, courtesy name [Youming], a native of [Yining in Jiangxi].
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen, whose courtesy name was Youming, was a native of Yining in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 少負志節，詩文皆有法度，為所器。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed firm resolve; his poetry and prose were all well regulated, and he was esteemed by Zeng Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had strong principles; his poetry and prose were disciplined, and Zeng Guofan valued him.

sentences.zh: 以舉人隨父治鄉團，禦寇。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he followed his father Weilin in organizing local militia to resist the Cantonese rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he followed his father Weilin in organizing local militia to resist the Taiping rebels.

sentences.zh: 已而走，參戎幕，軍、間。

translations.literal: He then went to Hunan and entered Yi Peishen's military staff, campaigning between Laifeng and Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Hunan and joined Yi Peishen's staff, campaigning between Laifeng and Longshan.

sentences.zh: 來犯，軍飢疲，走募糧，糧至不絕，守益堅，寇稍稍引去。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai attacked, the army was hungry and weary; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, and as supplies arrived without cease the defense grew firmer and the rebels gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai attacked, the army was hungry and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept arriving, the defense held firm, and the rebels gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 之，為畫策殲寇，事寧，敘知府，超授。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangxi he devised plans for Xi Baotian to destroy the bandit Hong Fuzhen; when the affair was settled he was rewarded with the rank of prefect and was exceptionally appointed to the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he helped Xi Baotian plan the destruction of Hong Fuzhen; when peace returned he was rewarded with the rank of prefect and was exceptionally appointed to the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 創，遴選三州學子，延名師教之。

translations.literal: He founded the Zhijing Academy, selected students from three prefectures, and invited distinguished teachers to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Zhijing Academy, chose students from three prefectures, and invited distinguished teachers to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner in Zhejiang and was dismissed because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner in Zhejiang and was dismissed because of a case against him.

sentences.zh: 巡撫薦其才，十六年，召入都，除按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: The Hunan governor recommended his talent; in the sixteenth year he was summoned to the capital, appointed surveillance commissioner in Hubei, and given acting charge of the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan governor recommended his ability; in the sixteenth year he was summoned to the capital, appointed surveillance commissioner in Hubei, and given acting charge of the provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢直隸布政使，入對，時東戰亟，見上形容憂悴，請日讀，以期變不失常。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili; on audience he found the emperor's appearance worn with care at the urgency of the war in the east, and urged daily reading of the Kangxi Emperor's annotated Book of Changes so that change might not depart from constancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to administration commissioner of Zhili; on audience, with the war in the east pressing hard, he saw the emperor worn with worry and urged him to read daily the Kangxi Emperor's annotated Book of Changes, so that in change he might not lose his footing.

sentences.zh: 他所陳奏語甚多，並稱旨。

translations.literal: His other memorial statements were many, and all pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His other memorials were numerous, and all pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以為忠，命治糈台，專摺奏事。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as loyal and ordered him to manage the grain depots and to submit memorials on special folded reports.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded him as loyal and ordered him to manage the grain depots and to submit memorials on folded reports reserved for the throne.

sentences.zh: 成，泣曰：「殆不國矣！

translations.literal: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was concluded he wept and said: "The state is nearly lost!
translations.idiomatic: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was concluded he wept and said: "The state is nearly lost!

sentences.zh: 」 明年，以薦，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: The next year, on Rong Lu's recommendation, he was promoted to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on Rong Lu's recommendation, he was promoted to governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 撫幕有者，植黨私利，至即重治之。

translations.literal: In the governor's staff there was Ren Lin, who formed a faction for private gain; as soon as Baozhen arrived he punished him severely.
translations.idiomatic: On the governor's staff was Ren Lin, who had formed a faction for private gain; as soon as Baozhen arrived he punished him severely.

sentences.zh: 布政使為關說，據以上聞，獲譴。

translations.literal: The Zhili administration commissioner Wang Lian interceded for him; Baozhen reported this to the throne, and Lian was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhili administration commissioner Wang Lian interceded for him; Baozhen reported this to the throne, and Lian was punished.

sentences.zh: 覆按被劾事，盡暴其任用非人狀，遂褫職。

translations.literal: When he re-examined the case in which Shi Nianzu had been impeached, he fully exposed Nianzu's employment of unfit men, and Nianzu was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When he re-examined the case against Shi Nianzu, he fully exposed how Nianzu had appointed unfit men, and Nianzu was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 繇是有伉直聲。

translations.literal: From this he gained a reputation for stern uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From this he gained a reputation for uncompromising uprightness.

sentences.zh: 俗故闇僿，思以一隅致富強，為東南倡，先後設電信，置小輪，建製造槍彈廠，又立保衛局、、。

translations.literal: Hunan custom was formerly benighted and narrow; Baozhen wished to make one corner rich and strong and be a leader for the southeast: he successively established telegraph lines, set up steam launches, built a factory for manufacturing firearms and ammunition, and also founded a defense bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had long been conservative and inward; Baozhen wished to make his province a model of wealth and strength for the southeast. He set up telegraph lines, steam launches, and a firearms factory, and also founded a defense bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.

sentences.zh: 延主學，俗大變。

translations.literal: He invited Liang Qichao to direct Hunan learning, and local custom changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Liang Qichao to direct Hunan learning, and local custom was transformed.

sentences.zh: 又疏請釐正學術及練兵、籌款諸大端，上皆嘉納，敕令持定見，毋為浮言動，並特旨褒勵之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting the rectification of scholarship and the major measures of drilling troops and raising funds; the emperor approved all and ordered him to hold to his settled views and not be moved by loose talk, and also issued a special edict praising and encouraging him.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on rectifying scholarship, drilling troops, and raising funds; the emperor approved all and told him to hold to his views and not be swayed by loose talk, and issued a special edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 是時負盛名，司道咸屏息以伺。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and all circuit intendants and prefects held their breath as they watched.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and all circuit and prefectural officials watched in silence.

sentences.zh: 初綰籓，遇事不合，獨與爭無私撓，雖不懌，無如何也。

translations.literal: When Baozhen first held the Hubei provincial administration commission, whenever matters did not agree he alone contended with Zhidong without private bias; though Zhidong was displeased, he could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen first held the Hubei administration commission, whenever they disagreed he alone argued with Zhidong without private bias; though Zhidong was displeased, he could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 久之，兩人深相結，凡條上新政皆聯銜，而撫反不與。

translations.literal: After a long time the two became deeply allied; whenever they memorialized on the new policies they signed jointly, while the Hubei governor Tan Jixun would not join them.
translations.idiomatic: In time the two became closely allied; memorials on the new policies were always signed jointly, while the Hubei governor Tan Jixun would not join them.

sentences.zh: 會言事數見效。

translations.literal: About this time Kang Youwei's memorials repeatedly took effect.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Kang Youwei's memorials repeatedly had effect.

sentences.zh: 素慕、薦士，因上言、、、佐新政。

translations.literal: Baozhen had long admired Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi in recommending men of talent, and therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: He had long admired Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi for promoting talent, and now memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.

sentences.zh: 上方詔求通變才，遽擢京卿，參新政，於是四人上書論時事無顧忌。

translations.literal: The emperor had just issued an edict seeking men of adaptable talent; the four were abruptly promoted to grand secretaries of the capital and took part in the new policies, and thenceforth memorialized on current affairs without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just called for men of adaptable talent; the four were abruptly promoted to capital grand secretaries and took part in the new policies, and thenceforth spoke on current affairs without reserve.

sentences.zh: 又言四人雖才，恐資望輕，視事過易，原得厚重大臣如者領之。

translations.literal: Baozhen also said that though the four had talent, he feared their standing was light and they would take office too easily; he wished that a weighty senior minister such as Zhang Zhidong might lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen also said that though the four had talent, their standing was light and they might take office too lightly; he wished that a weighty senior minister such as Zhang Zhidong might lead them.

sentences.zh: 疏上而太后已出訓政，誅四京卿，罪及舉主，去官，其子主事亦革職，並毀學所著、、、諸書。

translations.literal: The memorial had scarcely gone up when the Empress Dowager resumed regency; the four capital grand secretaries were executed, guilt reached the recommender, Baozhen was removed from office, his son the director Sanli was also dismissed, and the books written for Hunan studies—Regulations, Definitions, Notes, and Questions and Answers—were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial had scarcely gone up when the Empress Dowager resumed regency; the four capital grand secretaries were executed, guilt reached the man who had recommended them, Baozhen was removed, his son Sanli was also dismissed, and the books written for Hunan studies were all destroyed.

sentences.zh: 初，已革道員，以張揭帖攻西教為總督所治。

translations.literal: Earlier, the dismissed circuit intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor for posting broadsheets attacking Western religion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the dismissed circuit intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor for posting broadsheets attacking Western religion.

sentences.zh: 至，復刊帖傳布，令毀之，毆毀帖者，怒，下之獄。

translations.literal: When Baozhen arrived, Han again printed and circulated posters; Baozhen ordered them destroyed, Han beat those who destroyed the posters, Baozhen was angry and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen arrived, Han again printed and circulated posters; Baozhen ordered them destroyed, Han beat those who destroyed them, Baozhen was angry and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 舊黨恨次骨，然喜新之士，亦以此翕然稱之。

translations.literal: The old faction hated him to the marrow, yet men who favored the new learning also for this reason praised him with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: The old faction hated him to the marrow, yet men who favored reform also praised him warmly for this.

sentences.zh: 既去，諸所營構便於民者，雖效益已著，皆廢毀無一存雲。

translations.literal: After he left, all the institutions he had built for the people's benefit, though their good effects were already evident, were abolished and destroyed until not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, every institution he had built for the people's benefit, though their good effects were already clear, was abolished until not one remained.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 黃遵憲 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Huang Zunxian, courtesy name [Gongdu], a native of [Jiaying Prefecture].
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunxian, whose courtesy name was Gongdu, was a native of Jiaying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為道員。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased office and became a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he bought office and became a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 充使參贊，著上之朝。

translations.literal: He served as attaché on a mission to Japan and wrote the Record of Japan, which he presented to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attaché on a mission to Japan and wrote the Record of Japan, which he presented to the court.

sentences.zh: 旋移總領事。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to be consul-general at San Francisco.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to serve as consul-general at San Francisco.

sentences.zh: 吏嘗藉口衛生，逮僑滿獄。

translations.literal: American officials once used sanitation as a pretext and crowded Chinese sojourners into prison until it was full.
translations.idiomatic: American officials once used sanitation as a pretext and crowded Chinese sojourners into prison until it was full.

sentences.zh: 徑詣獄中，令從者度其容積，曰：「此處衛生顧右於僑居邪？

translations.literal: Zunxian went straight to the prison and had his attendants measure its capacity, saying: "Does sanitation here really take better care of health than where the sojourners live?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunxian went straight to the prison and had his attendants measure its capacity, saying: "Is sanitation here really better for health than where these people live?"

sentences.zh: 」吏謝，遽釋之。

translations.literal: The officials apologized and released them at once.
translations.idiomatic: The officials apologized and released them immediately.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽法道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He served on the Changbao salt circuit and held acting charge of the surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Changbao salt circuit and held acting charge of the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 時為巡撫，行新政，首倡民治於眾曰：「亦自治其身，自治其鄉而已。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Baozhen was governor and was carrying out the new policies; Zunxian was the first to advocate popular self-government to the people, saying: "It is simply to govern one's own person and govern one's own township."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Baozhen was governor and was carrying out the new policies; Zunxian was the first to advocate popular self-government to the people, saying: "It is simply to govern oneself and govern one's own township."

sentences.zh: 由一鄉推之一縣、一府、一省，以迄全國，可以成共和之郅治，臻大同之盛軌。

translations.literal: From one township extend to one county, one prefecture, one province, and then to the whole country—thus republican government at its best may be achieved and the grand path of Great Unity reached.
translations.idiomatic: From one township extend to one county, one prefecture, one province, and then to the whole country—thus the highest form of republican government may be reached and the grand path of Great Unity attained.

sentences.zh: 」於是略仿西國巡警之制，設保衛局，凡與民利民瘼相麗，而為一方民力能舉者，悉屬之，領以民望，而官輔其不及焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon, roughly imitating the Western system of police patrols, he established a defense bureau: whatever concerned the people's benefit or afflictions and could be undertaken by local popular strength was placed under it, led by men of local standing while officials supplemented where they fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, roughly imitating Western police patrols, he established a defense bureau: whatever served the people's welfare and could be undertaken by local effort was placed under it, led by men of local standing while officials supplemented where they fell short.

sentences.zh: 尋解職，奉出使之命，未行而黨禍起，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned his post and received orders to go abroad as envoy; before he could depart the factional disaster arose, and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned and received orders to go abroad as envoy; before he could depart the factional disaster broke out, and he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 著有等。

translations.literal: He wrote works including the Draft Poems from the Human Realm Studio and others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote works including the Draft Poems from the Human Realm Studio and others.

sentences.zh: 曾鉌 ，字，氏，正白旗人。

translations.literal: Zeng He, courtesy name [Huaiqing], of the Xitala clan, a bondservant of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng He, whose courtesy name was Huaiqing, of the Xitala clan, was a bondservant of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父，將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qingyun was general at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingyun was general at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 以任子為工部主事，累遷郎中，充軍機章京，轉御史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Works, was repeatedly promoted to bureau director, served as clerk in the Grand Council, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Works, rose to bureau director, served as clerk in the Grand Council, and was transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為督糧道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out as grain transport commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed grain transport commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 、各屬農民納糧例繳省倉，道塗艱遠，多弊竇，設法清釐之，民稱便。

translations.literal: In Xi'an and Tongzhou and their subordinate districts peasants paying grain tax were required by rule to deliver to the provincial granary; the roads were hard and long and there were many abuses; he devised methods to clear them up, and the people called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Xi'an and Tongzhou and their districts peasants paying grain tax were required to deliver to the provincial granary; the roads were long and abuses many; he devised methods to clear them up, and the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 士風樸僿，藝事苦窳，延、主書院，督課實學，士論翕然。

translations.literal: Scholarly custom in the capital region was plain and narrow and the arts were poorly cultivated; he invited Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangzan of Xianyang to direct the Guanzhong Academy, supervised instruction in practical learning, and scholarly opinion united in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly custom in the capital region was plain and narrow and the arts poorly cultivated; he invited Bo Jingwei and Liu Guangzan to direct the Guanzhong Academy, supervised practical learning, and scholarly opinion united behind him.

sentences.zh: 又設蠶桑局，聘織師教以煮湅織染法，歲出絲帛埒、。

translations.literal: He also established a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach boiling, reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year silk and cloth were produced equal to Qi and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He also established a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach boiling, reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year produced silk and cloth rivaling Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，母憂解職。

translations.literal: The next year, on mourning for his mother, he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起故官，俄遷布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed he was recalled to his former office and soon promoted to provincial administration commissioner in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former post and soon promoted to administration commissioner in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調，迴避，留本任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili but withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest and remained in his present post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili but withdrew for avoidance and remained in his present post.

sentences.zh: 擢巡撫，慨然曰：「時艱至此，猶可拘成法不變耶？

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Hubei and said with feeling: "The times are hard to this point—can we still cling to established rules and not change?"
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Hubei and said with feeling: "The times are hard to this point—can we still cling to established rules and refuse to change?"

sentences.zh: 」於是假總督印上陳補官、掣籤、度支、訟獄四事，宜變通成例，厚植國本。

translations.literal: Thereupon, using the Shaan-Gan governor-general's seal, he memorialized on four matters—filling offices, drawing lots, revenue, and litigation—urging that established precedents be flexibly changed to strengthen the foundations of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, using the Shaan-Gan governor-general's seal, he memorialized on filling offices, drawing lots, revenue, and litigation, urging that established precedents be flexibly changed to strengthen the state.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士、光祿寺少卿彈其亂政，詔褫職。

translations.literal: Reader in waiting Yi Gu and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for disordering government, and an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Reader in waiting Yi Gu and vice minister Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for disordering government, and an edict stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 始，官京朝，家綦貧，僦居陋室。

translations.literal: At first, when he held office in the capital, his family was extremely poor and he rented a mean dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when he held office in the capital, his family was extremely poor and he rented a mean dwelling.

sentences.zh: 及任外台，孜孜民事，不顧問有無。

translations.literal: When he held office in the provinces he worked tirelessly at the people's affairs and did not ask whether he had means or not.
translations.idiomatic: When he served in the provinces he worked tirelessly at the people's affairs and never troubled himself over his own means.

sentences.zh: 既閒廢，出入皆徒步，民恆歲醵金濟之。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed he went everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly collected money each year to support him.
translations.idiomatic: After he was dismissed he went everywhere on foot, and the people of Shaanxi regularly pooled money each year to support him.

sentences.zh: 後益困，至敝衣鬻卜都市。

translations.literal: Later he grew still poorer, until he wore ragged clothes and sold divination in the market of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he grew still poorer, until he wore ragged clothes and sold divination in the capital markets.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 改元，總督為奏復原官。

translations.literal: When the reign title was changed, Governor-General Duan Fang memorialized to restore his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed, Governor-General Duan Fang memorialized to restore his former rank.

sentences.zh: 楊深秀 ，字，本名，人。

translations.literal: Yang Shenxiu, courtesy name Yicun, original name Yuxiu, a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenxiu, whose courtesy name was Yicun and whose original name was Yuxiu, was a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 少穎敏，諳西算術。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and clever and was versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was quick and clever and was versed in both Chinese and Western mathematics.

sentences.zh: 初，以舉人入貲為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate he purchased office and became an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as a provincial graduate he purchased office and became an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 假歸，值大饑，銜命籌賑，條上改革差徭法，困少蘇。

translations.literal: On leave at home he encountered a great famine; Yan Jingming was charged with organizing relief, and Shenxiu memorialized on reforming the corvée system, so distress was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: On leave at home he encountered a great famine; Yan Jingming was charged with organizing relief, and Shenxiu memorialized on reforming the corvée system, so distress was somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 十五年，成進士，就本官遷郎中，轉御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he passed the jinshi examination, was promoted from his present office to bureau director, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he passed the jinshi examination, was promoted from his present post to bureau director, and was transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「時勢危迫，不革舊無以圖新，不變法無以圖存。

translations.literal: He once said: "The times are perilously pressing; without reforming the old there is no way to seek the new, and without changing the laws there is no way to seek survival."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "The times are perilously pressing; without reforming the old there is no way to seek the new, and without changing the laws there is no way to seek survival."

sentences.zh: 」 二十四年，人脅割、。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Russians compelled the cession of Port Arthur and Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the Russians compelled the cession of Port Arthur and Dalian Bay.

sentences.zh: 深秀力請聯、拒之，詞甚切直。

translations.literal: Shenxiu strongly urged allying with Britain and Japan to resist them, his language very earnest and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu strongly urged allying with Britain and Japan to resist them, in language that was very earnest and direct.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷銳意行新政，而大臣恆多異議。

translations.literal: At that time the court was keen to carry out the new policies, but high ministers often had many objections.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was keen to carry out the new policies, but high ministers often raised objections.

sentences.zh: 乃與先後疏請定國是，又以取士之法未善，請參酌、、舊制，釐正文體，下其議於禮部，尚書心非之，未奏也。

translations.literal: He and Xu Zhijing then memorialized in succession requesting that the national policy be settled; he also held that the method of selecting scholars was not good and asked that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted to rectify literary forms; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites, whose minister Xu Yingkui disapproved in his heart and did not report upward.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu Zhijing memorialized in succession to settle the national policy; he also argued that the examination system was flawed and asked that Song, Yuan, and Ming precedents be consulted to rectify literary forms; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites, whose minister Xu Yingkui disapproved but did not report upward.

sentences.zh: 會議經濟特科務減額，於是合彈其阻撓。

translations.literal: When the special examination in political economy was discussed with a view to reducing the quota, Shenxiu and Song Bolu jointly impeached Xu for obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the special examination in political economy was discussed with a view to reducing the quota, Shenxiu and Song Bolu jointly impeached Xu for obstruction.

sentences.zh: 上令自陳，奏上，劾​​夤緣要津，請罷斥，詞連，上不之詰也。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xu to explain himself; when his memorial went up he impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed, his words implicating Shenxiu, but the emperor did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xu to explain himself; when his memorial went up he impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed, implicating Shenxiu as well, but the emperor did not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 御史劾傳布有為所立，並暴交通內外狀，責以代人報復，反獲咎。

translations.literal: Censor Wen Ti impeached Shenxiu for spreading the Society to Preserve the Nation founded by Kang Youwei and also exposed Kang's communications inside and outside the court; the emperor rebuked Wen for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wen himself was blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wen Ti impeached Shenxiu for spreading Kang Youwei's Society to Preserve the Nation and exposed Kang's communications inside and outside the court; the emperor rebuked Wen for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wen himself was blamed.

sentences.zh: 益感奮，連上書請設譯書局，派王公遊歷各國，並定遊學章程，皆報可。

translations.literal: Shenxiu was all the more stirred and sent repeated memorials requesting the establishment of a translation bureau, the dispatch of princes and dukes to travel in various countries, and the fixing of regulations for study abroad; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu was all the more stirred and sent repeated memorials requesting a translation bureau, the dispatch of princes and dukes to travel abroad, and regulations for study overseas; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 又請試庶官，日番二十人，料簡貞實，而汰其庸愚罷老不諳時務者，繇是廷臣益側目。

translations.literal: He also asked to examine ordinary officials, twenty each day in rotation, to select the upright and solid and weed out the mediocre, foolish, aged, and those ignorant of current affairs; from this court ministers watched him all the more askance.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to examine ordinary officials, twenty each day in rotation, to select the upright and weed out the mediocre, foolish, and aged who were ignorant of current affairs; from this court ministers watched him all the more askance.

sentences.zh: 巡撫圖治甚急，中蜚語，為剖辨之，上以特旨褒，乃得行其志。

translations.literal: The Hunan governor Chen Baozhen was governing with great urgency and was slandered; Shenxiu explained the matter for him, and the emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, who was then able to carry out his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Baozhen of Hunan was governing with great urgency and was slandered; Shenxiu explained the matter for him, and the emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, who was then able to carry out his aims.

sentences.zh: 八月，政變，舉朝惴惴，懼大誅至，獨抗疏請太后歸政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the political change occurred; the whole court was fearful, dreading great punishments, but Shenxiu alone submitted a defiant memorial asking the Empress Dowager to return power.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the coup occurred; the whole court was fearful, dreading mass executions, but Shenxiu alone submitted a defiant memorial asking the Empress Dowager to return power.

sentences.zh: 方疏未上時，其子苦口諫止，厲聲叱之退。

translations.literal: When the memorial had not yet gone up, his son Futian earnestly admonished him to stop; Shenxiu sternly shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial went up, his son Futian earnestly admonished him to stop; Shenxiu sternly shouted at him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 俄被逮，論棄市。

translations.literal: Soon he was arrested and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was arrested and sentenced to public execution.

sentences.zh: 性鯁直，嘗面折人過，以此叢忌。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and upright and would often rebuke others' faults to their faces; for this he gathered many enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and upright by nature and often rebuked others to their faces, which won him many enemies.

sentences.zh: 官臺諫十閱月，封事二十餘上，稿不具存，惟獄中詩三章流傳於世。

translations.literal: He held censorial office for ten months and submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts do not all survive, but three poems written in prison have circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He held censorial office for ten months and submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts do not all survive, but three poems written in prison have circulated.

sentences.zh: 著有、。

translations.literal: He wrote works including Drafts from the Hall of Empty Voices and the New Gazetteer of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote works including Drafts from the Hall of Empty Voices and the New Gazetteer of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 楊銳 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Yang Rui, courtesy name Shujiao, a native of Mianzhu in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui, whose courtesy name was Shujiao, was a native of Mianzhu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 少俊慧，督學奇其才，招入幕。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and gifted; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong admired his talent and took him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever and gifted; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong admired his talent and took him into his staff.

sentences.zh: 肄業，年最少，嘗冠其曹。

translations.literal: He studied at the Zunjing Academy, was the youngest in years, and often led his class.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Zunjing Academy, was the youngest in his class, and often ranked first.

sentences.zh: 優貢朝考得知縣。

translations.literal: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the capital examination and was appointed district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the capital examination and received appointment as district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 督，從赴。

translations.literal: When Zhidong was governor of the two Guang provinces, Rui followed him to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhidong was governor of the two Guang provinces, Rui followed him to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，舉順天鄉試，考取內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，薦應經濟特科。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Zhidong recommended him to sit for the special examination in political economy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Zhidong recommended him to sit for the special examination in political economy.

sentences.zh: 又以薦，與、、並加四品卿，充軍機章京，參新政。

translations.literal: He was again recommended by Chen Baozhen and, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu, was all given the rank of fourth-grade grand secretary, appointed clerk in the Grand Council, and took part in the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen also recommended him, and together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu he was given the rank of fourth-grade grand secretary, appointed clerk in the Grand Council, and took part in the new policies.

sentences.zh: 召見，面陳興學、練兵為救亡策，稱旨。

translations.literal: On audience he stated in person that promoting education and drilling troops were strategies to save the state, and pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On audience he stated in person that promoting education and drilling troops were strategies to save the state, and pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 七月，禮部主事上封事，尚書等格不奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the director Wang Zhao of the Ministry of Rites submitted a sealed memorial, but Ministers Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Director Wang Zhao of the Ministry of Rites submitted a sealed memorial, but Ministers Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not present it.

sentences.zh: 上聞，震怒，盡褫尚書侍郎六人革職，朝臣皆不自安。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was greatly angered and stripped all six ministers and vice ministers of office; court officials were all ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he was greatly angered and stripped all six ministers and vice ministers of office; court officials were all ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 上手詔密諭云：「近日朕仰觀聖母意旨，不欲退此老耄昏庸大臣而進英勇通達之人，亦不欲將法盡變。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote a secret edict to Rui saying: "Recently I have observed the Empress Dowager's intentions: she does not wish to remove these aged, muddled, and incompetent ministers and advance brave and penetrating men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote a secret edict to Rui saying: "Recently I have observed the Empress Dowager's intentions: she does not wish to remove these aged, muddled ministers and advance brave and penetrating men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely."

sentences.zh: 朕豈不知積弱不振，非力行新政不可？

translations.literal: Do I not know that long weakness cannot be roused, and that the new policies must be vigorously carried out?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that long weakness cannot be roused without vigorously carrying out the new policies?

sentences.zh: 然此時不惟朕權力所不及，若強行之，朕位且不能保。

translations.literal: Yet at this time not only is my power insufficient; if I force the matter through, I cannot even preserve my throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this moment my power is not enough; if I force reform through, I cannot even keep my throne.

sentences.zh: 爾與、、等詳悉籌議，必如何而後能進用英達，使新政及時舉行，又不致少拂聖意，即具奏，候朕審擇，不勝焦慮之至！

translations.literal: You and Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the rest must deliberate in full detail how outstanding men can be advanced so that the new policies may be carried out in time and yet not offend the Empress Dowager's mind in the least; memorialize at once and await my careful choice. I am overcome with anxious distress!
translations.idiomatic: You and Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the rest must deliberate fully on how outstanding men can be advanced so that the new policies may be carried out in time without offending the Empress Dowager; memorialize at once and await my choice. I am overcome with anxious distress!

sentences.zh: 」復奏言：「太后親挈大位授之皇上，皇上宜以孝先天下，遇事將順。

translations.literal: Rui memorialized again: "The Empress Dowager personally bestowed the great throne upon Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all under Heaven and yield to circumstances in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Rui memorialized again: "The Empress Dowager personally bestowed the throne upon Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all under Heaven and yield to circumstances in affairs."

sentences.zh: 變法宜有次第，進退大臣不宜太驟。

translations.literal: Reform should proceed in stages, and the advancement or dismissal of high ministers should not be too sudden.
translations.idiomatic: Reform should proceed in stages, and the advancement or dismissal of high ministers should not be too sudden.

sentences.zh: 」上是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 已而太后再訓政，諸言新政者皆予重誅。

translations.literal: Before long the Empress Dowager resumed regency, and all who had spoken for the new policies were given heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Empress Dowager resumed regency, and all who had spoken for the new policies were given heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 既下獄，自揣實無罪，謂即訊不難白，次日，遽詔與等同棄市。

translations.literal: After he was imprisoned he reckoned himself truly innocent and thought that once questioned he would easily be cleared; the next day an edict suddenly ordered him to be executed in the marketplace together with Liu Guangdi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: After he was imprisoned he reckoned himself truly innocent and thought that once questioned he would easily be cleared; the next day an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Liu Guangdi and the rest.

sentences.zh: 改元，子繳手詔於都察院，請代奏，始傳於世。

translations.literal: When the reign title was changed, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the handwritten edict to the Censorate and asked that it be presented on his behalf; only then did it circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the handwritten edict to the Censorate and asked that it be presented on his behalf; only then did it circulate.

sentences.zh: 劉光第 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Liu Guangdi, courtesy name Peicun, a native of Fushun in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangdi, whose courtesy name was Peicun, was a native of Fushun in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 治事精嚴，因讞獄忤長官​​，遂退而閉戶勤學，絕跡不詣署。

translations.literal: He handled affairs with strict precision; because of a criminal case he offended his superior and therefore withdrew, closed his door, studied diligently, and no longer set foot in the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He handled affairs with strict precision; because of a criminal case he offended his superior, withdrew, closed his door to study diligently, and no longer set foot in the yamen.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，而性廉介，非舊交，雖禮饋弗受。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor, yet his nature was incorruptible; except for old friends he would not accept gifts even of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been poor, yet his nature was incorruptible; except for old friends he would not accept gifts even of courtesy.

sentences.zh: 獨與善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms only with Yang Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms only with Yang Rui.

sentences.zh: 通、及。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Greater and Lesser Records of the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Greater and Lesser Records of the Rites.

sentences.zh: 其應召也，亦以薦，然非其素志，將具疏辭，人官京朝者力勸之。

translations.literal: When he was summoned he too was recommended by Chen Baozhen, yet this was not his lifelong wish; he was about to prepare a memorial declining, but Sichuan men holding office in the capital strongly urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned he too was recommended by Chen Baozhen, yet this was not his lifelong wish; he was about to prepare a memorial declining, but Sichuan men holding office in the capital strongly urged him on.

sentences.zh: 一日，召見，力陳時危民困，外患日迫，亟宜虛懷圖治，上稱善。

translations.literal: One day on audience he strongly stated that the times were perilous, the people distressed, and foreign danger pressing daily; he urgently urged open-minded planning for good government, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: One day on audience he strongly stated that the times were perilous, the people distressed, and foreign danger pressing daily; he urgently urged open-minded planning for good government, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 惟時言路宏啟，臣民奏事日數百計，竟日批答，簽識可否，以待上裁。

translations.literal: At that time the channels of remonstrance were broadly opened and officials and people submitted affairs by the hundreds each day; Guangdi spent the whole day annotating approvals or rejections to await the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the channels of remonstrance were broadly opened and officials and people submitted affairs by the hundreds each day; Guangdi spent the whole day annotating approvals or rejections to await the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 退語所親曰：「吾終不任此，行當亟假歸矣！

translations.literal: On retiring he said to those close to him: "I can never bear this burden; I shall soon ask leave to return home at once!"
translations.idiomatic: On retiring he said to those close to him: "I can never bear this burden; I shall soon ask leave to return home at once!"

sentences.zh: 」未一月而禍作，自投獄。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed disaster struck, and he gave himself up to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed disaster struck, and he gave himself up to prison.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，協辦大學士監斬，詫曰：「未訊而誅，何哉？

translations.literal: At the execution Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading; Guangdi exclaimed in surprise: "To be put to death without interrogation—how can this be?"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading; Guangdi exclaimed in surprise: "To be put to death without interrogation—how can this be?"

sentences.zh: 」令跪聽旨，不可，曰：「祖制，雖盜賊，臨刑呼冤，當復訊。

translations.literal: He was ordered to kneel and hear the decree but would not, saying: "By ancestral institution, even for thieves, if at execution they cry out their innocence, they must be re-examined."
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to kneel and hear the decree but would not, saying: "By ancestral institution, even for thieves, if at execution they cry out their innocence, they must be re-examined."

sentences.zh: 吾輩縱不足惜，如國體何！

translations.literal: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!"

sentences.zh: 」默不應，再詢之，曰：「吾奉命監刑耳，他何知​​？

translations.literal: Gangyi was silent and did not answer; when asked again he said: "I am ordered to supervise the execution—that is all I know."
translations.idiomatic: Gangyi was silent and did not answer; when asked again he said: "I am ordered to supervise the execution—that is all I know."

sentences.zh: 」獄卒強之跪，崛立自如。

translations.literal: The jailers forced him to kneel, but he stood erect as before.
translations.idiomatic: The jailers forced him to kneel, but he stood erect as before.

sentences.zh: 呼曰：「，跪！

translations.literal: Yang Rui called out: "Peicun, kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui called out: "Peicun, kneel!

sentences.zh: 跪！

translations.literal: Kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Kneel down!

sentences.zh: 遵旨而已。

translations.literal: It is only to obey the decree."
translations.idiomatic: It is only to obey the decree."

sentences.zh: 」乃跪就戮。

translations.literal: Only then did he kneel and submit to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he kneel and submit to execution.

sentences.zh: 著有。

translations.literal: He wrote the Collected Prose and Poetry of the Jiebai Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Collected Prose and Poetry of the Jiebai Studio.

sentences.zh: 譚嗣同（唐才常） ，字，人。

translations.literal: Tan Sitong (Tang Caichang), courtesy name Fusheng, a native of Liuyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Sitong (with Tang Caichang), whose courtesy name was Fusheng, was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父，巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Jixun was governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jixun was governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，文為奇肆。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and had great ambitions; his writing was strange and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was free-spirited and ambitious; his writing was bold and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 其學以日新為主，視倫常舊說若無足措意者。

translations.literal: His learning took daily renewal as its principle and regarded old doctrines of ethics and constancy as scarcely worth a thought.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took daily renewal as its principle and regarded old doctrines of ethics and constancy as scarcely worth a thought.

sentences.zh: 素謹飭，以是頗見惡。

translations.literal: Jixun had always been strict and cautious, and for this was rather disliked by Sitong.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun had always been strict and cautious, and for this Sitong rather disliked him.

sentences.zh: 乃遊幕，以同知入貲為知府，銓。

translations.literal: Sitong then traveled on Liu Jintang's staff in Xinjiang, purchased office as an associate prefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong then traveled on Liu Jintang's staff in Xinjiang, purchased office as an associate prefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 撫，還鄉佐新政。

translations.literal: When Chen Baozhen became governor of Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baozhen became governor of Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.

sentences.zh: 倡辦，為之長。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao proposed establishing the Southern Study Society, and Sitong became its head.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qichao proposed establishing the Southern Study Society, and Sitong became its head.

sentences.zh: 屆會期，集者恆數百人，聞慷慨論時事，多感動。

translations.literal: When meetings were held several hundred people regularly gathered; hearing Sitong speak passionately on current affairs, many were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When meetings were held several hundred people regularly gathered; hearing Sitong speak passionately on current affairs, many were moved.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，召入都，奏對稱旨，擢四品卿、軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned to the capital; his audience pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to fourth-grade grand secretary and clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned to the capital; his audience pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to fourth-grade grand secretary and clerk in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 四人雖同被命，每召對，建議獨多。

translations.literal: Though the four received the same appointment, whenever they were summoned to audience Sitong's proposals were the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Though the four received the same appointment, whenever they were summoned to audience Sitong's proposals were the most numerous.

sentences.zh: 欲開，設顧問官，令擬旨，必載明前朝故事，將親詣請命太后。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to open the Maojin Hall and establish advisory officials; he ordered Sitong to draft edicts, which had to cite clearly precedents from former reigns, and was about to go in person to the Summer Palace to request the Empress Dowager's approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to open the Maojin Hall and establish advisory officials; he ordered Sitong to draft edicts, which had to cite clearly precedents from former reigns, and was about to go in person to the Summer Palace to request the Empress Dowager's approval.

sentences.zh: 退謂人曰：「今乃知上絕無權也！

translations.literal: Sitong withdrew and said to others: "Now I know that the emperor has no power at all!"
translations.idiomatic: Sitong withdrew and said to others: "Now I know that the emperor has no power at all!"

sentences.zh: 」時督，以監司練兵。

translations.literal: At that time Rong Lu was governor-general of the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai was drilling troops at Tianjin as a surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Rong Lu was governor-general of the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai was drilling troops at Tianjin as a surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔擢侍郎，召入覲。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Yuan Shikai to vice minister and summoned him to audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Yuan Shikai to vice minister and summoned him to audience.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜詣有所議。

translations.literal: Sitong once went to Yuan Shikai by night to discuss matters with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong once went to Yuan Shikai by night to discuss matters with him.

sentences.zh: 明日，返天津。

translations.literal: The next day Yuan returned to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuan returned to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 越晨，太后自還宮，收政權。

translations.literal: The following morning the Empress Dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the Forbidden City and took back political power.
translations.idiomatic: The following morning the Empress Dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the Forbidden City and took back political power.

sentences.zh: 避匿日本使館，往見之，勸東遊。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation; Sitong went to see him and urged him to travel east.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation; Sitong went to see him and urged him to flee east.

sentences.zh: 曰：「不有行者，無以圖將來；

translations.literal: Sitong said: "Without those who go, there is no way to plan for the future;
translations.idiomatic: Sitong said: "Without those who go, there is no way to plan for the future;

sentences.zh: 不有死者，無以酬聖主。

translations.literal: without those who die, there is no way to repay the sage ruler."
translations.idiomatic: without those who die, there is no way to repay the sage ruler."

sentences.zh: 」卒不去。

translations.literal: In the end he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not leave.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斬於市。

translations.literal: Before long he was beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 著有及等。

translations.literal: He wrote works including Benevolence and the Collected Poems of the Mangcang Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote works including Benevolence and the Collected Poems of the Mangcang Studio.

translations.literal: Tang Caichang, courtesy name Fochen.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Caichang, whose courtesy name was Fochen.

sentences.zh: 少與齊名，稱「二生」，高材生也。

translations.literal: In youth he was equally famous with Sitong and was called "the two students of Liuyang"; he was a gifted student of the Two Lakes Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was equally famous with Sitong and was called "the two students of Liuyang"; he was a gifted student of the Two Lakes Academy.

sentences.zh: 聞死，憂憤，屢有所謀，每言及，常泣下。

translations.literal: When he heard of Sitong's death he was grief-stricken and angry, plotted repeatedly, and whenever he spoke of Emperor Dezong would often weep.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of Sitong's death he was grief-stricken and angry, plotted repeatedly, and whenever he spoke of Emperor Dezong would often weep.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮出狩，陰結謀舉事，號勤王，將攻、。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two palaces went on tour, he secretly joined the Society of the Wealthy to plot an uprising, called it "loyal service to the throne," and was about to attack Wuchang and Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two palaces went on tour, he secretly joined the Society of the Wealthy to plot an uprising in the name of loyal service to the throne and was about to attack Wuchang and Hankou.

sentences.zh: 被獲，慷慨言無所隱，請就死，遂殺之。

translations.literal: He was captured, spoke boldly without concealment, asked to die, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was captured, spoke boldly without concealment, asked to die, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 林旭 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Lin Xu, courtesy name Dungu, a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xu, whose courtesy name was Dungu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉本省鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At nineteen he took first place in the provincial examination of his province.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he took first place in his province's civil examination.

sentences.zh: 後試禮部，值構釁，糾同試者上書論時事，不報。

translations.literal: Later he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination; when the Sino-Japanese conflict arose he rallied fellow candidates to submit a memorial on current affairs, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took the metropolitan examination; when war broke out between China and Japan he rallied fellow candidates to submit a memorial on current affairs, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased office and became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased office and became a secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時倡言變法，先於京師立，以振厲士氣，而、、、諸會繼之。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei advocated reform and first established the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to rouse scholarly spirit, and the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian study societies followed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kang Youwei advocated reform and first established the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to rouse scholarly spirit, and the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian study societies followed.

sentences.zh: 為領袖，又充會員。

translations.literal: Lin became leader of the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Society to Preserve the Nation as a member.
translations.idiomatic: Lin became leader of the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Society to Preserve the Nation.

sentences.zh: 先為將軍，雅好士，及至，延入幕。

translations.literal: Rong Lu had earlier been general at Fuzhou and always favored Fujian scholars; when he reached Tianjin he took Lin into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu had earlier been general at Fuzhou and always favored Fujian scholars; when he reached Tianjin he took Lin into his staff.

sentences.zh: 俄以奏保人才召見，操土語，上不盡解。

translations.literal: Soon, on memorial recommendation of talent, he was summoned to audience; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor did not fully understand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to audience on a memorial recommending talent; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor did not fully understand.

sentences.zh: 退繕摺，上稱善，遂命與等同參機務，詔諭多起草。

translations.literal: On retiring he drafted a folded memorial; the emperor praised it and then ordered him to take part in confidential affairs together with Tan Sitong and the rest; many edicts were drafted by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: On retiring he drafted a folded memorial; the emperor praised it and ordered him to take part in confidential affairs with Tan Sitong and the rest; many edicts were drafted by Lin.

sentences.zh: 及變起，同戮於市，年二十有四。

translations.literal: When the coup broke out he was executed in the marketplace together with the others, aged twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup broke out he was executed in the marketplace with the others, at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 著有。

translations.literal: He wrote the Collected Poems of the Late Emerald Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Collected Poems of the Late Emerald Studio.

sentences.zh: 妻孫女，聞變，仰藥不死，以毀卒。

translations.literal: His wife was a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen; when she heard of the disaster she took poison but did not die, and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen; when she heard of the disaster she took poison but did not die, and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 康廣仁 ，名，以字行，弟。

translations.literal: Kang Guangren, personal name Youpu, known by his courtesy name, younger brother of Kang Youwei.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guangren, whose personal name was Youpu and who was known by his courtesy name, was the younger brother of Kang Youwei.

sentences.zh: 少從兄學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 上書請改革，謂當先變科舉，庶人才可出。

translations.literal: When Youwei memorialized requesting reform, Guangren said the civil service examinations should be changed first, so that talent might emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When Youwei memorialized requesting reform, Guangren argued that the examinations should be reformed first if talent was to emerge.

sentences.zh: 其後罷鄉會試、製藝，而歲科試未變，激勵言官抗疏論之，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: Thereafter the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the examination essay were abolished, but the annual county examination had not yet changed; Guangren urged censors to submit defiant memorials on the matter, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the eight-legged essay were abolished, but the annual county examination had not yet changed; Guangren urged censors to submit defiant memorials, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 於是語：「今科舉既廢，宜且南歸興學專教育，俟養成多數有用才，數年後乃可云改革也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangren said to Youwei: "Now that the examinations are abolished, you should return south for the time being and devote yourself to education, wait until many useful men have been trained, and only after several years speak of reform."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Guangren told Youwei: "Now that the examinations are abolished, you should return south for the time being and devote yourself to education, wait until many useful men have been trained, and only after several years speak of reform."

sentences.zh: 」不忍去。

translations.literal: Youwei could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei could not bring himself to leave.

sentences.zh: 及初聞變，復趣歸。

translations.literal: When he first heard of the coup, Guangren again urged him to return.
translations.idiomatic: When he first heard of the coup, Guangren again urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 走，被逮。

translations.literal: Youwei fled; Guangren was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei escaped; Guangren was arrested.

sentences.zh: 在獄言笑自若，臨刑猶言曰：「自強之機在此矣！

translations.literal: In prison he spoke and laughed as usual; at execution he still said: "China's opportunity for self-strengthening lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: In prison he spoke and laughed as usual; at the execution he still said: "China's opportunity for self-strengthening lies here!"

sentences.zh: 」 【論曰】 論曰：戊戌變法，發憤圖強，用等言，召用新進。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the reform of the wuxu year Emperor Dezong, stirred by indignation, sought to strengthen the state, followed the counsel of Li Duanfen and others, and summoned and employed new men.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In the wuxu reform Emperor Dezong, stirred by indignation, sought to strengthen the state, followed the counsel of Li Duanfen and others, and summoned new men to office.

sentences.zh: 百日維新，外震仰，黨爭遽起，激成政變。

translations.literal: For a hundred days the new policies were maintained; China and foreign countries looked up in awe; factional struggle suddenly arose and provoked the political coup.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred days the new policies were maintained; China and foreign countries looked on in awe; factional struggle suddenly arose and provoked the coup.

sentences.zh: 、、、及、同日被禍，世稱「六君子」，皆悲其志。

translations.literal: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, and Shenxiu and Guangren suffered execution on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, Shenxiu, and Guangren were executed on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.

sentences.zh: 內爭不已，牽及外交。

translations.literal: Internal struggle did not cease and drew in foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: Domestic strife did not end and soon entangled foreign relations.

sentences.zh: 其後遂釀庚子排外之亂，終致危亡。

translations.literal: Afterward this brewed the gengzi anti-foreign turmoil and in the end brought peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward this led to the anti-foreign turmoil of the gengzi year and in the end brought the dynasty to ruin.

sentences.zh: 此亦代興衰一大關鍵也。

translations.literal: This too was a great turning point in the rise and fall of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: This too was a great turning point in the rise and fall of the Qing dynasty.
